title: Static Members and Friends
summary: A **static member** belongs to the **class itself** and is shared by all its objects. A **friend** is a function or class that has been granted access to another class's private members.
ideas:
1. Give a `Bullet` class a static count of live bullets and a static `maxBullets` constant.
2. Add the factory functions `Color::fromHex(std::uint32_t)` and `Color::fromRgb(int, int, int)`.
3. Write a friend function `bool sameBalance(const Account& a, const Account& b)`.

cards.q: Can a static member function use non-static members?
cards.a:
No, it has no `this` pointer

A static member function belongs to the class, not to an object, so there is no object whose members it could use.

cards.q: If `A` declares `B` a friend, can `A` access `B`'s private members?
cards.a:
No, friendship is one-way

`A` lets `B` see `A`'s private members. For `A` to see `B`'s, `B` would have to declare `A` a friend too.

cards.q: How many copies of a static member variable exist if ten objects are created?
cards.a:
One, shared by all of them

A static member variable belongs to the class. All objects share the single copy.

A function, often static, that creates and returns an object with a descriptive name

Factories such as `Color::fromHex(...)` say *how* the object is made, which several constructors with similar parameters cannot.
